body: The game’s most wanted criminal, no NPC in Probably Stolen can rival or challenge the mysterious (& dangerous) Lou.

And as you can expect, her cryptic persona persists in her quest, which can only be triggered and completed by playing a dangerous game. Here’s a full walkthrough on how to complete the Lou storyline in Probably Stolen .
Probably Stolen Lou quest walkthrough

Unlike most NPCs, like Serpico and Eleanor , Lou only appears on a random day after you purchase the Business Permit, available in the fifth week. During her visit, she will introduce herself before asking you for a series of ”tools” to be used on her next job. To trigger her quest and start her storyline, call Security on her and claim the 1.500 Credits bounty.

Screenshot by Destructoid Now that you surprised Lou and made the questionable choice of turning in a specialist, a Republic Operative will pay you a visit in the next week, claiming Lou to be a traitor to the Republic and an alleged terrorist. He also gives you a Republic Transmitter and makes an offer: plant it into something and give it to Lou for 700 Credits, as she is sure to visit you again.

Screenshot by Destructoid Sure enough, Lou will surprise you in a few weeks, inviting you to play a game and letting you know what’s at stake. The next morning, she reveals that a bomb is hidden within your wares and gives you until midnight to disarm it. Upon review, the Plastic Explosive will prove to be fake.
Screenshot by Destructoid Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !

Following your fake brush with death, Lou will pay a visit to the store in around five days and leave her ”Box of Toys” in your care, before warning you not to touch it. The box features a document revealing more about her past and ties with the Republic.

She returns to grab it the next day. If you haven’t moved the contents of the box (you can still read the document at no risk) or placed the transmitter in it, she allows you to pick either 1x Advanced Turbo Booster, 1x Smuggler’s Bay, 1x Backpack (Small), or 2x Module Expansion Kits as a reward.

Screenshot by Destructoid Following the encounter above, just keep playing until Lou visits under the guise of an inspector. She reveals that her ”guest’ has finally given her the info she needs, before asking for 750 Credits (or 500 depending on your chosen difficulty) worth of weapons, armor, or meds as a trade for the bounty you received earlier. You have one week to secure it. If you can’t, she asks for the amount in Credits on the due date.

Screenshot by Destructoid We are now at the final stretch of her storyline, as Lou will thank you and vanish upon getting the agreed-upon ”tools” (or the necessary Credits) in her next visit. This will be your final meeting, with the news of the assassination of an admiral stamping the papers the next morning. She will send you a note, though, together with a Storage Bay Expansion Kit.
Screenshot by Destructoid Lou’s quest/storyline then ends with another visit from the Republic Operative, who reveals they plan to pursue her and hints at your involvement in the whole ordeal.
With Lou’s quest done, don’t forget to also check out how to produce Huge Nutrifruits and unlock the Green Thumb achievement .

articles.headline: Timberwolves reportedly sign ex-76ers 6-foot-10 versatile forward to potentially carve out key role
keyFacts: The past few months have been a whirlwind for Johni Broome, both on and off the court.

body: The past few months have been a whirlwind for Johni Broome, both on and off the court. The former Auburn star has bounced around the NBA, experiencing the business side of the league as he searches for an opportunity to establish himself. For some players, that means moving from team to team in hopes of finding the right situation to jump-start their professional careers.
Broome began the summer as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. However, he was later traded to make room for LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.

“The Philadelphia 76ers are trading C/F Johni Broome and a second-round pick to the Los Angeles Clippers for cash considerations, sources tell ESPN. The deal allows the 76ers to stay under both first and second aprons while signing LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

Broome's time with the Los Angeles Clippers didn't last long, as the team eventually waived him. He then signed a training camp deal with the Milwaukee Bucks, but was among several players who were let go as Milwaukee continued trimming its roster.

“The Milwaukee Bucks have requested waivers on Pete Nance, Johni Broome and Jake Stephens as the team continues to reduce its roster ahead of the 2026-27 NBA regular season,” ClutchPoints’ Abdullah Imran wrote.

Now, Broome has another opportunity, this time with one of the Western Conference's biggest contenders. On Wednesday, the nearly seven-foot center agreed to a two-way deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

“The Minnesota Timberwolves and Johni Broome have agreed to a two-way deal, league sources told hoopshype. The former SEC Player of the Year and consensus All-American was the 35th overall pick of the 2025 NBA Draft and spent last season with the Philadelphia 76ers,” HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto wrote.

This is a valuable opportunity for the former SEC Player of the Year. With injuries potentially opening up opportunities, Broome could have a chance to carve out a role in Minnesota. The two-way contract also allows the Timberwolves to add him without using a standard roster spot, while still giving him an opportunity to contribute at the NBA level.

After a hectic few months, Broome will be hoping to find some stability and a place where he can settle in. Of course, nothing is guaranteed with a two-way contract, but he remains an intriguing developmental piece for Minnesota.
Why the Timberwolves signed Broome

Minnesota has a need for additional frontcourt depth, and signing Broome to a two-way contract is a relatively low-risk move because it does not guarantee him a standard roster spot. The organization also sees potential in the former Auburn standout and can use this opportunity to continue developing his game.

Broome still has plenty of room to grow, and Minnesota will have the chance to see what he can bring to the organization. Being waived by three teams in just a few months could also give him extra motivation to make the most of this opportunity.

Overall, Broome has several qualities that make him an intriguing prospect, including his seven-foot wingspan. Minnesota may not need him to contribute every night, but he could provide valuable minutes when called upon.

body: While the Tampa Bay Rays lost in the World Series to the Milwaukee Brewers, the 2026 season was a great one for the franchise. Looking ahead, the Rays still have work to do.
The roster has some issues worth addressing, but the Rays haven't typically been big spenders, so managing where they spend their money will be a key storyline this offseason.

Heading into the offseason, according to Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo of The Athletic, the Rays have shown an interest in signing 2.67 ERA All-Star ace Drew Rasmussen to a contract extension that will likely be very costly.
Rays interested in signing Drew Rasmussen to contract extension
"The Tampa Bay Rays hold interest in keeping their ace Drew Rasmussen beyond the upcoming season, people familiar with the club's thinking said," The Athletic trio reported.

Currently, Rasmussen is only signed through the 2027 MLB season on a one-year, $20 million contract. That's a lot of money for one season for the Rays, so it wouldn't be a surprise if Rasmussen were a trade candidate.

While they could trade him, the Rays are instead interested in signing him to a long-term contract extension. Rasmussen is one of the game's best starters, and locking him up for the next few seasons would be a sensible move.

It will surely cost a lot, potentially more than $20 million per-year. But considering the dominance of Rasmussen, with his 2.67 ERA this past season fresh in the Rays' memory, a big-money deal is worth making.

A long-term deal at a very high price tag might not be in the Rays' normal offseason plans, but Rasmussen is a special case and is someone the Rays might finally be willing to extend to a long-term contract.

The team should feel similarly about Junior Caminero, a young superstar who is more than worth signing to a massive long-term deal. With the MLB salary landscape set to change in the near future, spending a lot on Rasmussen would make sense.

At some point, the Rays do need to sign good players to big deals if they want to continue contending. Rasmussen, the 31-year-old right-handed ace, is someone the team should be willing to break the bank for. And their interest shows they might be ready to do just that.

articles.headline: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?
keyFacts: Jensen Huang has resigned, and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress.
But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea.
Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013.
body: Jensen Huang has resigned, and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress.
But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea.

Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013. That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18.
Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then.

Generally, Kress has stayed out of any contentious issues with the company, only occassionally commenting on the big issues during earnings calls. Like when the RTX 30-series was out of stock everywhere thanks to cryptocurrency mining (the mining had an impact on the company's financials in a slightly contentious way, too).

Or ceaseless comments on the increasing demand for AI datacentre build out. That's of less interest to gamers, but what do you expect? Nvidia to talk about gaming GPUs in this day and age? It cannot be done.
In an email to employees in the wake of Jensen Huang's departure, Kress reportedly said (via Hadas Gold on X):
The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products
"I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.

"The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.

"... We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company."

Kress also notes there will be a company meeting on November 18—the day after Nvidia's next financial call, which Kress will have been preparing for in her CFO role, and the day of Jensen Huang's meeting with US House leaders.

Kress will have been chosen for this interim CEO role in some part to steady the markets. It takes a long time to find and finalise a deal to secure a new full-time CEO, especially with a job opening as internationally as important as this one. So someone inside the company had to take the chalice for now. With Kress at the helm, Nvidia will be hoping investors won't be quite as worried about the company's financial future.

It's the same playbook we saw when Intel ousted then-CEO Brian Krzanich over a consensual relationship he had with an employee, which was against company policy. Krzanich was replaced by Bob Swan as interim CEO, who actually took over as CEO at a later date, before Pat Gelsinger took over from him in 2021. Pat then retired in 2024.

Nvidia will likely look at this as a bit of a cautionary tale: you want stability and leadership, not a revolving door of top execs and no one steering the ship. If the board has any wits about it, it'll be looking for a strong leader with a clear direction for the company and the will to deliver it.
President Donald Trump has come out in support of a man who only just managed to escape top corporate life at Apple: Tim Cook.
Meanwhile the China Select Committee in US Congress backs any leader that "makes national security its top priority."
So, a true patriot that can also lead teams of top-class engineers and wants to fill the boots of a man that famously didn't take breaks. That'll be easy to find, I'm sure.

articles.headline: Manchester United receive huge injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash
keyFacts: Manchester United receive huge injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in ahead of Liverpool trip Manchester United have pulled the trigger on Michael Carrick.
After 10 league matches, they sit 18th in the Premier League, with one win all season.
That is the hard reality, and ultimately it cost him his job.
body: Manchester United receive huge injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in ahead of Liverpool trip

Manchester United have pulled the trigger on Michael Carrick. After 10 league matches, they sit 18th in the Premier League, with one win all season. That is the hard reality, and ultimately it cost him his job.

The dismissal came during the international break, after a run of results that left little room for debate. A club statement said United had concluded that a change was necessary after a disappointing start to the season. They had just lost 3-0 to Bournemouth, 2-0 at Chelsea and 4-1 away to Como in the Champions League. Even the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa did more to underline the chaos than offer encouragement. United were 2-0 and 4-2 down before late goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point.
That leaves United in their lowest position after 10 top-flight games since 1986-87. For a club with their budget and expectations, that is grim reading.
Pochettino lined up for Old Trafford

Carrick only took over in January, following Ruben Amorim’s departure, and did enough to earn the job full time. He guided United to third place and Champions League qualification, then signed a contract until 2028 in May. He lasted 173 days after that deal was agreed.

Mauricio Pochettino is now close to becoming the next Manchester United manager. An outline agreement is reportedly in place with the current United States coach, and a framework has been agreed with US Soccer. His contract extension from three months ago includes a $10 million release clause, and he is expected to be in charge for the trip to Anfield, although no appointment had been confirmed at the time of writing.
Marcus Rashford injury latest before Liverpool

One possible boost before Liverpool is Marcus Rashford. United are hopeful the forward can be available after beginning a new treatment programme. He travelled to Dublin last week with a member of the club’s medical staff to consult a groin specialist, and a revised recovery plan is now in place.

Rashford returned to Old Trafford in the summer after a year on loan at Barcelona, having suffered a hip injury at the World Cup. He featured in United’s first six league games, the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton and the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in mid-October. He then aggravated the problem, and it spread to his groin.

He has missed the last six matches. His record against Liverpool gives United some reason to push for his return quickly. Rashford has scored seven goals against them in his career, including in FA Cup wins in 2021 and 2024.
Anfield now frames the next step

For United, everything now points to Anfield. New manager, possible return for Rashford, and a table that already looks ugly. There is no time for sentiment. Carrick paid for poor results, and whoever comes next inherits a mess that needs fixing quickly.

articles.headline: Carrick sacked by Manchester United with team in Premier League relegation zone – live
keyFacts: Michael Carrick has been dismissed by Manchester United.
He departs after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford last Sunday that left the team in the Premier League’s bottom three.
United twice fought back from two goals down for a late point against Villa, after a dramatic recovery to defeat Roma in the Champions League five days earlier, but that wasn’t enough.
body: Michael Carrick has been dismissed by Manchester United. He departs after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford last Sunday that left the team in the Premier League’s bottom three. United twice fought back from two goals down for a late point against Villa, after a dramatic recovery to defeat Roma in the Champions League five days earlier, but that wasn’t enough.

United are third-bottom in the Premier League, a point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and 17th in the Champions League league phase table. His departure follows a review led by the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy.
It was telling that Pochettino did a sit-down with a few select UK journalists in September. The clue was there, perhaps. But it’s not Tottenham, it’s Manchester United. Well, probably.

Pochettino’s situation, though, does feel different with the longer contract – certainly to him. “Now it is a different thing,” he says. “When we gave our word to the federation [in August 2024], it was about starting and finishing after the World Cup. For us, it was the moment to say: ‘If some club comes, it’s impossible.’ Always you can break a contract, say you stop and that’s it … you agree something. But in the moment it wasn’t right for us to create all these situations and expectations.

“Now it’s a four-year contract, it’s different. We can next season lose the Copa América or the Gold Cup, they’re not happy with us and they can sack us. Or we can say: ‘OK. It’s not in the way that we think.’ Four years is different. Maybe now if someone calls in the future, it’s a different, different type [of thing]. We are excited, we are thinking to spend four years to the next World Cup. But now it’s a long period.”

On Tuesday, Antonee Robinson, the USMNT player previously linked to Manchester United, had this to say on the Pochettino links: “As a soccer player, we’re pretty used to sort of fast training environments and games … so we’re all very good at just focusing on the next task and about the next session or the next game coming up. For me personally, I don’t really look at it … It’s just focusing on we’ve got a game at the weekend and I’m going to do everything I can to be ready to play for him, and how he wants us to play.”
David Wall gets in touch: “I think there was a quote from Ferguson earlier on the blog about United managers having to play one game on the pitch and another off it, with the media.

“But given the extent of coverage and scrutiny that the club are under nowadays, is it possible for one person to manage that second game alone, let alone manage it as well as what is happening on the pitch. United seems like no other club in this country, perhaps anywhere other than Madrid and Barcelona.

“After all, I don’t remember a blog when Liverpool sacked Slot, or when Maresca left Chelsea, for example. And at which other club would the contract status of a youth- team player without a first team game to his name be national news? And that scrutiny inevitably filters into the dressing room (Maguire mentioned after the game against Ipswich, I think, that they could sense that the crisis calls wouldn’t be far off if they’d not won that game (turns out it only postponed them)). How can anyone play, let alone manage, in those conditions?”
Jack Grealish has made an Everton comeback by playing in a friendly behind closed doors against Derby. He is visible in an Instagram picture in an official club post.
Ahead of the game against Coventry, David Moyes was asked if there was a chance of Grealish coming back: “Of course there is, yes.”

Joshua Keeling gets in touch: “Here’s my take: Carrick succeeded in the second half of last season off the back of the fitness and tactical work Amorim did with the squad. They were so much fitter under Amorim, and that’s fallen off a cliff this season.

”It’s the right decision to let him go. He’s still a club legend and one of us, and the fans still love him, but it wasn’t working. Pochettino will probably fail as well, given the issues at United. But he gives us a better chance. He’s a club builder, the club just need to equip him to do it.”
Gary Neville has had his say, as you might expect, telling Sky Sports News:

“I think after the Bournemouth game I said at the time that Manchester United effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch at the end of the game with that lap around, that wave goodbye. I think he was expecting it to come at that point and they were indecisive.

“They obviously felt that they might be able to get to the international break and there could be some sort of pick-up in results, but it’s been a difficult two weeks. Indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership.

“In the last 24-48 hours it’s been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who’s a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership. I don’t think anybody comes out of this well at all.”

Folarin Balogun, the USMNT striker, has been asked about Pochettino: “If it’s something that becomes official, then he will let us know,” Balogun said on a video call from the U.S. camp ahead of the team’s double-header against Haiti.
“If I had a vote,” Balogun added, in reference to Pochettino’s future, “I would like to keep things the way they are.”

Ben Monroe-Lake is back in touch: “After my last email, Manchester’s finest men are back to make more good decisions. Pochettino isn’t going to arrive until just before their match at Liverpool? Fantastic. Genius. Inspired. Is Pochettino the answer? No idea, maybe? He could probably need more than a few days to organise himself in a new ground, in a different country and city for sure though.”

Interesting quote from Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe in 2024: “We’ll decide that [playing] style, plus the CEO, sporting director, probably the recruitment guys; what the style of football is, and that will be the Manchester United style of football, and the coach will have to play that style.

“We’re not going to oscillate from a (Jose) Mourinho style to a (Pep) Guardiola style. That’s not the way we’ll run the club. Otherwise, you’re changing everything all the time; you change your coach, you’ve got the wrong squad — we won’t do that. In modern football, you need to decide what’s your path and stick to your path.”
Krishna gets in touch: “Let us look at the upside. Everyone knows what is wrong at OT and everyone agrees that nothing can be done, so we might as well look at some pluses.

“Any red card will be rescinded immediately- this will make the players bold and make them approach the D which is treated as dementors colony right now. Facing Chelsea and Tottenham will be candy. They will get all the juices. Players and fans can take a picture with Poch and have it framed as ‘When I met Russell Crowe’.”

Pochettino managing the USMNT for those two games is very Manchester United 2026. Our estimation in the office is he lands at Ringway Airport on Thursday from Cincinnati, when some of his players will be back from international duty the day before. Darren Fletcher taking training again? Or will Carrick keep turning up?

US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino will lead the US through the remainder of the current international window, a source with direct knowledge of US Soccer’s plans told the Guardian on Thursday.

Pochettino has emerged as the leading candidate to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked as United manager on Thursday. The Guardian previously reported that the framework of a deal had been agreed between Pochettino and United. The Athletic were first to report news of Pochettino’s plans for the upcoming US matches.

The USMNT face Haiti on Saturday and then again on Tuesday in Miami and Cincinnati, respectively, in the quarter-final of the Concacaf Nations League. Pochettino has been leading the US through training at the federation’s headquarters and training facility outside Atlanta since early this week. The Argentine has yet to publicly address his link to Manchester United, though he is scheduled to meet with the press on Friday morning.
There was, of course, another Premier League sacking today.

Sage has been walking a tightrope since the 5-0 thrashing at Brighton last month when it was made clear to the 47-year-old that he must tighten a defence that had conceded the most goals in the Premier League. Some players are thought to have questioned his training methods, although Dean Henderson, the captain, was among those believed to have pledged their support for Sage after defeats by Newcastle and Tottenham.

David Flynn gets in touch: “Hi John, I must say I don’t fully agree that United keep appointing yesterday’s men, they’ve also tried appointing tomorrow’s men (Amorin, Ten Haag) and nobody’s men (Carrick, Ole). It’s actually a broad spectrum of mistakes that they keep making.”

Ben Monroe-Lake gets in touch: “We live in an age of incredibly powerful individuals, people who wield vast amounts of money and influence and increasingly make little attempt to hide how readily they are to fling such influence and money around for their own benefit. Trump, Musk, Huang, Zuckerberg etc.

“And yet at the same time, these people seem entirely unable to not show everyone their arse, on ever more impressive stages, in ever more shocking ways. So the mind trust at Manchester United are a particularly great microcosm of this. Men of a particular age, who voluntarily took up this position, wrested control of the football operations in fact, as they thought they could do it better. Yet it’s obvious how bad they are at this, even without seeing inside their Monaco based boardrooms.

“Extend Ten Hag’s contract based on the performance in one game. Force in a young manager with a rigid tactical plan without the players to support it. Fire the person you paid Newcastle Utd a huge fee to hire, because he points out this is stupid. Keep on the interim manager with little experience and don’t fill the most gaping holes in his squad.
“In between this, fire the tea ladies, make some questionable pronouncements and who can even remember all the gaffes.

“Of course it’s slightly terrifying that people who are essentially “in charge” are so stupid but it’s a little bit mollifying that people that seem happy to wade waist deep into all aspects of our lives are as dumb as I am. All that really separates me from them is luck and being more willing to get up at five in the morning. So perhaps one day someone not a total bozo will make enough money to buy a football club.”

David Wall gets in touch: “One thing that concerns me about Pochettino is how he will engage with the academy. There was a lot made when he was at Spurs about how he favoured young players. But in fact most of those young players were bought in from outside of the club. It was only Kane from their academy who became a regular in the first team (perhaps with Winks, although more as a squad player rather than first choice). Is Pochettino the type of manager who will spend his midweek evenings going to watch the youth sides play, or is he just going to give an instruction about age-profile to the recruitment department?”

Winks started the 2019 Champions League final, as did Kane, rather unfortunately. At Chelsea, there was definite friction with the club hierarchy, though the signs at United are that he could have the personality to create his own powerbase. Within United, there is a great big vacuum that someone needs to fill.

The problem with Pochettino is that he’s very much the face of 2015 rather than 2026, setting aside what was a decent enough USMNT World Cup until it all went wrong. United keep doing this. Louis van Gaal would have been a fine appointment in 1996 rather than 2015, and Jose Mourinho would have been ideal in 2003, rather than 2016. Of course, United had a good manager in those days but times move on.

Joe Taylor gets in touch: “Spurs fan here. I’m a bit confused by the Pochettino-Spurs revisionism. Sometimes managers don’t get credit for taking players that until that point hasn’t achieved anything and turning them into world beaters (eg. Eriksen, Son) but in this case he doesn’t even get credit for players that didn’t do anything before or after his tenure (eg. Dier, Dele Alli, Dembele, Lamela). I’d suggest he had quite a large hand in that squad that supposedly made his life easy. I think he’s perfect for United right now.”
I’d agree. He made the most of what he had, and a player of a couple of players who have achieved very little without his help. There’s a few projects to work on at United.
Warning: Poch may not be an instant cure for the Manchester United malaise.

At Chelsea, just one win from his first six league games, same at Southampton and Espanyol, while at Tottenham he won two and drew two. At PSG, he won four of his first six games, which at that club is probably below par.
The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST) earlier issued a statement following Carrick’s dismissal pinning the blame for poor results firmly on the ownership. In full below:

Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United. We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.

The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.
They lie with the ownership.
The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.
It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability.
But the discontent at United is not just about matters on the pitch. Far from it.

Aggressive ticketing policies have further damaged relations with supporters. Treating loyal fans principally as a source of revenue undermines their identity and the bond with the team that sustains support through difficult times. Supporters are being asked to pay the price for the owners’ mismanagement as well as their stadium ambitions through higher charges and diminished rights.

The earlier Stretford End banner declaring “The way you treat us is a disgrace” was a warning. The unprecedented scale of the booing at Old Trafford, alongside public criticism from senior players in recent weeks, now points to a deeper deterioration. These are signs of a club becoming more divided, with the bond between supporters, players and those running Manchester United under increasing strain.

MUST warned publicly in January 2025 that alienating supporters risked a downward spiral of worsening atmosphere, performances and financial outcomes. Our subsequent Telegraph article urged Sir Jim Ratcliffe to break that “doom loop” by bringing supporters with him. Those warnings remain painfully relevant.

The owners must allow senior club management to change direction: show accountability, rebuild trust, listen to supporters and recognise that their loyalty is fundamental to football success. Another change of head coach cannot repair what the ownership continues to undermine.
The pattern is repeated, the problems remain the same. Wrote this a couple of weeks ago.

Beyond Busby and Ferguson, each United manager who also served felt the lash of desperation of a falling giant. Each of their defenestrations has featured an infighting that would not have been out of place in ancient Rome. Favouritism, nepotism, self-interest, entitlement, complacency and sentimentality have been the betrayal of a legend, to use the title of Michael Crick’s and David Smith’s “j’accuse” book from 1989. Living with the legend and influence of those two managers leads the list of difficulties.

United fans know such history too well. “You lousy bastards, you let him down,” Brian Kidd told teammates when the bullet came for Wilf McGuinness, Busby’s immediate successor, in December 1970. Busby himself had done the deed. A December 1972 meeting at Selhurst Park with Tommy Docherty as Crystal Palace beat United 5-0 hastened the end for Frank O’Farrell.

An email! “I’m a lifelong Spurs fan and enjoyed having Poch as manager,” writes Alan. “But he did have a squad that made his life pretty easy. By the start of his second season, 2015-16, he could field this side: Lloris; Walker, Alderweireld, Vertonghen, Rose; Eriksen, Dier, Dembele; Dele Alli, Kane, Son. Not sure how many of the current United squad would get into that team. Sadly most of them would also get into the current Spurs team!”

The timing of Pochettino’s expected arrival will be interesting. The US men’s side have a Concacaf Nations League game against Haiti in Kingston, Jamaica, on Saturday, with the return leg next Wednesday in Cincinnati. Manchester United travel to Anfield in the Premier League four days later.
The nitty gritty of that is surely forming part of the conversations ongoing now. Either way, US Soccer will be quids-in as Jeff Rueter explains here.

The real boon is his release clause, a reported $10m (£7.5m) option that only a Big Club could afford to spring. Had Pochettino left after the World Cup, coach and federation would have parted with nothing more exchanged than a handshake and some pleasantries. Instead, they forged an insurance policy to make up for what could have been if Pochettino had stayed for a full cycle.

How do you solve a club that has won two major trophies in 10 years of steady downward progress? Easy. You hire a coach who has also won two major trophies in 13 years of steady downward progress. How do we get back to the dimly remembered recent past? We hire the dimly remembered recent past.
Does this feel like a magic bullet? At this stage hiring Pochettino is like booking the bloke who did Gangnam Style to play the Super Bowl. Yeah, huge fan. Remind me. Weren’t you quite big in 2013?

What next for Michael Carrick is also an interesting question. Has he done enough to put himself in contention for the next Premier League vacancy that comes up? Or is it back to the Championship, where his tenure with Middlesbrough was mixed to say the least? With Regis Le Bris and Matthias Jaissle probably looking the least secure in the top flight at the moment, might a return to the north east be on the cards at some point for the Wallsend-born man? Doesn’t feel quite right, does it? But you never know.

Hello all. Perhaps the most immediate problem facing Mauricio Pochettino when he arrives will be playing personnel. It’s painfully obvious – and is has been for years – that where once Manchester United was home for the best of the best, these days it’s … not. Everyone has their own view on players but when you look at the teamsheets for the key recent games against Aston Villa, Chelsea and, yes, Bournemouth you’d be hard-pressed to suggest that United had a truly superior 20-man matchday squad for those games. And Pochettino isn’t going to be able to fix that overnight.

You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago.

And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants”, to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie.

“Michael Carrick has been at the helm during the Red Devils’ first dip into the relegation zone since 1986 yet somehow is also definitely not at fault. There is almost total agreement on the latter point, that United’s issues are structural and systemic and absolve Carrick of blame. Still, he’s gotta go, because what can you do, eh?”

“Pochettino who built something at Tottenham despite the environment,” Daniel writes of the Argentinian in that piece below “… the sense is that, as when Mourinho arrived at Old Trafford after years of speculation, he’s past his magical best.”

In January 2014 the 13th series of Celebrity Big Brother aired in the UK, the show so popular that its run time was extended by five days before a public vote anointed Jim Davidson the winner. Then, two years later when Brexit happened, people wondered where their tolerant country had gone, lamenting the ephemeral spirit of London 2012 as though the 2011 riots were some kind of fever dream, not a desperate response to decades of structural and institutional racism exacerbated by the cruelty of unnecessary austerity.

The truth is that if security is quickly upended, it was built on quicksand to begin with. Which brings us to Manchester United, easing effortlessly from an uplifting third-place finish to some of the worst football in their history.

It is entirely possible that Alex Ferguson made a deal with the devil to the effect that United would be great until he retired and hilariously dreadful thereafter. But assuming not, his l’état, c’est moi mentality was busy setting up the post-him fall even at the height of the success – itself a consequence of what had gone before.

articles.headline: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
keyFacts: Trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US, and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended without a ceasefire but yielded a prisoner exchange agreement.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff traveled to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he wants to coordinate positions with the United States following the Moscow meeting.
body: The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia said a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy."
How significant is the prisoner swap?
Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.
"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," says Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing."
A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.
Empty diplomacy without a real breakthrough?

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.
Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases."
Experts: chances for Russia-Ukraine ceasefire low as things currently stand

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.
Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist says.
Redrawing borders to make Putin feel like a winner?

Ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on new US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia."
Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov said the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.
"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov said.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.
Putin demands large swaths of Ukrainian territory

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.
"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

The expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.
Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

"Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.
What next after Abu Dhabi?

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been announced so far.
Iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the issue is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.
This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

articles.headline: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
keyFacts: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang was forced out of his role following allegations of workplace affairs.
Colette Kress will temporarily lead Nvidia, a company whose advanced chips drive the artificial intelligence industry.
An investigation into Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy will continue to determine his future.
body: - Published
If I'd told you this time last week that Jensen Huang was about to leave Nvidia, you would not have believed me.

The man who co-founded this enormously successful AI chip company, working tirelessly to build it from the ground up and steering it through some disastrous times with endless energy and ruthless determination, has ultimately been undone by his own love life.
It's an extraordinary tale and a strangely old fashioned one for a tech firm with its sights set on the future.

It spawned a plethora of viral memes, seeing Huang as the man caught by the Coldplay kiss-cam with a married colleague, or singing along to George Michael's classic hit about betrayal, Careless Whisper.
Both were ironically AI-generated using the very tech he was helping to build.
This week I met two Silicon Valley execs and I asked them how they were processing the news - "in memes", was the response.
But they didn't seem to think Huang would be forced out by his alleged adultery.
The stakes were too high, they said, the entire AI industry relies too heavily on Nvidia chips to break a winning formula.
In as many words, "the Valley" was on his side.
But that was before rumours of a second affair surfaced, this time with a colleague, and the board decided he had gone too far.
His behaviour suddenly cast him in a different light: a man who could make bad decisions and cover them up.
Long hours and competitive spirit
Huang always made a point of standing out from the crowd.
During the coronavirus lockdowns, he streamed keynote speeches from his kitchen (which gained internet fame in its own right, but were later revealed to have been AI-generated).
He is rarely seen without a leather jacket â he has joked that he only owns one suit, and he borrows his daughter's partner's tie.
Huang rubbed shoulders with the elite, with a network including Donald Trump, Elon Musk and King Charles.
The last time I saw him was at St James' Palace last year, where he was receiving the prestigious Queen's Prize for Engineering.

I was told he would not talk to the press - but he wandered over by himself and we spent about 10 minutes having a chat while press officers hovered nervously in the background. He was articulate and optimistic about the progress of AI and the UK's role in it.
For many people, Huang was Nvidia. He had as many as 200 people directly reporting to him.
He expected high standards â in his book about its inner workings, the Nvidia Way, author Tae Kim wrote the office hours were long
Huang's feedback could be both brutal and public, and he thought nothing of pointing out individuals' mistakes in all-staff meetings.
Now it is his own shortcomings which are on very public display, and he has been forced into a brutal ending of his own career.
Nvidia without Huang
Colette Kress, who takes over for now, will be a familiar face internally and that must feel reassuring to some at Nvidia.

She's worked at the firm for 13 years and for those who follow the firm's considerable finances, she is often present on earnings calls. She is a billionaire in her own right and a high-flying tech exec.
But she's not an engineer and Nvidia's products are highly technical.

She will have to convince investors that it is business as usual for Nvidia, that the innovation for which it is renowned can continue at its existing pace, and that the top talent won't leave with Huang.
A wobbly Nvidia would be bad news for the entire AI industry because its ever-advancing chips drive the most powerful AI models.

As for Huang himself, we assume for now that the investigation into his relationship with the woman accused of being a Chinese spy will continue, and the results of that may well determine what he does next.

He probably won't be short of offers despite his conduct â and I expect Nvidia's rivals can't believe their luck that their formidable rival has taken himself out of the game. Elon Musk has already said it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.
It's important though to remember that even if Huang turns out not to have betrayed his company or his country, he still betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang.
And for her, it's not a story of tech, temptation and trillion-dollar-valuations.
It's a painfully personal matter.

articles.headline: Trump lays out his lame-duck agenda, and it sounds familiar
keyFacts: Donald Trump posted Truth Social updates threatening doubled tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop an incoming migrant caravan.
Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to focus on blue-state corruption, pulling Vance away from diplomatic talks regarding Iran.
Trump's legislative agenda depends on a Congress he no longer fully controls and expected incoming Democratic investigations.
body: Welcome to Thursday’s edition of Washington Secrets. Today we run the rule over Donald Trump’s early morning Truth Social posts, which feature some of his greatest hits. Plus, we keep an eye on what could be a nice little Republican feud brewing. And we have more of your thoughts on whether JD Vance should run for the top job.
Did Donald Trump just set out the agenda for his lame-duck years?
Recommended Stories

Starting at 5:50 a.m. with a Truth Social attack on Democrats as they prepare to launch a slew of investigations into his administration, the president went on to tackle Iran, fraud, border security, and his tax returns.

He ordered his vice president to take on blue-state corruption, threatened Mexico with sanctions if they fail to stop migrants crossing into the United States, and lamented the ability of Senate Republicans to pass his SAVE America Act.
In other words, it amounted to a selection of his greatest hits, reprising old themes and shifting blame for last week’s electoral disaster.

“With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms – I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again,” he said in one post. “Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico.”
He said he would double tariffs on Mexico if it failed to prevent the caravan reaching American soil.

The group is estimated to be 1,500 strong. It set off from the southern city of Tapachula on Tuesday, and members told reporters they hoped the Democrats’ victories might open the door to a new life in the U.S.
Could Trump’s own words also have signaled a softening of position? In a 60 Minutes interview broadcast on Sunday, he signaled what conservative allies worried might be an immigration “amnesty.”

“Get the killers out. Get the rapists out. Get all the rough ones out. Get the drug dealers out,” Trump said when pushed by interviewer Ross Douthat to explain whether his deportation policies may have gone too far. “But let the people that are here, and in some cases here for 10 and 15 years, work a deal for them, OK?”
That approach didn’t last long. Soon after the interview was recorded on Friday, Trump announced that he was installing immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff.

Either way, his Truth Social screed marks a return to the rhetoric that helped him win a sensational election victory in 2024, and which became obsolete with the success of his border security policies.
In another post, Trump underlined his administration’s war on fraud, pulling JD Vance away from Iran talks.

“I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.,” the president wrote.

That removes an odd wrinkle from Trump’s foreign policy. He said the war was “effectively over” after meeting with Qatar’s prime minister this week, at the same time that Vance was exploring ways to negotiate an end to the conflict with hard-liners in Tehran.
But perhaps his first order of business is to shore up defenses against an expected Democratic onslaught of investigations.

“Now, in order to deflect from MASSIVE BLUE STATE CORRUPTION & CRIME, they are at it again, illegally threatening Republicans with knowingly false accusations and charges,” he posted. “Other than cheating, this is how they won the Midterms – But we won’t let our Country go to hell!”
Whether any of it becomes policy will now depend on a Congress he no longer fully controls, and on investigators who have not yet started.
His agenda is a series of posts. The test is what happens after he stops typing.

You are reading Washington Secrets, a guide to power and politics in D.C. and beyond. It is written by Rob Crilly. You can reach him at secrets@washingtonexaminer.com with your comments, story tips, and suggestions.
A Schlapp down
Matt Schlapp, the conservative power player who runs the CPAC gatherings, took a rather pointed shot at Mick Mulvaney on X yesterday.

Mulvaney was installed as acting White House chief of staff in 2019, and held the post for about a year. He then became special envoy for Northern Ireland but resigned after the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol.

Schlapp’s dig that he was only ever an “acting” chief of staff is perhaps a reminder that we are seeing Republican battle lines harden between an old guard and Trump loyalists as officials deal with the midterm wipeout.
What should Vance do?

Earlier this week we ran a straw poll of Trumpworld insiders and MAGA types on whether they believed Vance will run in 2028 and, perhaps more importantly, whether he should run. (Broadly, respondents said they think he will run but were much more mixed on whether it was a wise idea).

Responses are still coming in, and here are a couple more that show some of the doubts about whether he is the right man and whether this is the right time for any Republican to take a tilt at the top job.

Respondent (Yes – will run/No-shouldn’t run): “I think his response on Iran made him look weak. He acknowledged where the voters are at, but he failed to act to push the admin to not make a major policy decision. His team hasn’t made the case for where JDV really stood so currently he doesn’t look like he’s as strong as he should be.“

“[Secretary of State Marco] Rubio meanwhile lingered back at the perfect time. In a time when the GOP base is fractured and frustrated as hell, we need someone who can pull younger voters back and the Hispanic coalition. Rubio has time and time again shown he’s eloquent, diplomatic but also means business.”

Respondent (Y/Y): “In 250 years, just 45 individuals have served as president. Of course, he should take his shot, as he may never get another chance. But only four sitting vice presidents have won the presidency, and just one in the last 190 years.”
Whether or not Rubio wades into the race might be the key question hanging over what is increasingly likely to be a crowded Republican primary.
Lunchtime reading

Kraft Heinz has a comeback plan – Cheesy ramen and high-protein Jell-O: But what would RFK Jr. make of Crystal Light with extra fiber and protein, or sandwich bacon? These are supposed to be health-oriented, yet they seem uber-processed.
The Left’s election denial: As ever, it is the extremes that attract the headlines and attention. Yet the hard Left actually won the smallest swings in the midterm elections.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress
keyFacts: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving after lawmakers threatened to subpoena him, Chairman Brian Mast said.
Huang stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.
The testimony will take place behind closed doors and is expected to be recorded and transcribed, Chairman Brian Mast said.
body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News.

Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.

The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees. Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

articles.headline: Trump floats Tim Cook as next Nvidia CEO
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
President Donald Trump suggested Tim Cook replace Huang, while Nvidia CFO Colette Kress serves as interim CEO.
Incoming Senate committee chair Elizabeth Warren stated that Democrats plan to interrogate Huang regarding national security risks.
body: President Donald Trump suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after he abruptly resigned Thursday morning.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on Truth Social .
It’s not clear whether Trump suggested Cook as a joke. Trump last week joked that he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House press secretary position.
Huang resigned after embarrassing reports that he had two extramarital affairs with a suspected spy for China and Kimberly Powell, a company employee who reported to him.
U.S. officials reportedly believe Alice Huang exploited the romantic relationship with Huang to gather intelligence for Beijing.
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, will serve as the company’s CEO while the company searches for a permanent replacement.
Nvidia is best known for its artificial intelligence chips and controls about 90% of the market. The stunning allegations against Huang have sent the company’s shares plunging.

Trump was reportedly told about Huang’s relationship with the spy, but it’s not clear what, if any, action was taken. Officials believe that Huang and Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where she worked, helped smuggle restricted chips into China.
The president will travel to China next week but has said he does not intend to raise the Nvidia affair with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
NVIDIA’S JENSEN HUANG RESIGNS AFTER CONFESSING TO AFFAIR WITH SUSPECTED CHINESE SPY
Democrats, however, plan to interrogate Huang over his actions once the 120th Congress is sworn in.

“NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s decision to resign does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws,” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), the incoming chairwoman of the Senate banking committee, in a statement.

articles.headline: Ukraine says military Starlink disrupted again as US envoys meet Putin in Moscow
keyFacts: President Zelensky said restrictions on Starshield satellite services are currently disrupting Ukraine's military operations against Russian drones.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow regarding ending the war in Ukraine.
The US envoys are expected to travel to Dublin next to meet with Zelensky.
body: - Published

President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Ukraine's military is again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv is struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.
It came as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky told European leaders in Dublin that Ukraine was trying to clear up the Starlink situation with the American side.

But he added "some things" were already clear: "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going."
He did not elaborate further.
Starshield was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use. Along with Starlink, it has come to play a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

A similar issue with connectivity affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before it was fixed. It remained unclear who had ordered the temporary restrictions on Starlink services at the time, with US officials and SpaceX offering differing explanations.
Zelensky said the current disruption had been ongoing for several days and was "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine".
Kushner and Witkoff are expected to travel to Dublin to meet Zelensky after their meeting with Putin.
Videos shared by Russian media on Thursday showed the US representatives disembarking a plane and being welcomed by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev with handshakes and hugs.
Later, they headed to the Kremlin where they met Putin and three of his senior advisors.

In remarks broadcast by Russian media, Putin asked the US envoys to convey his "gratitude" to US First Lady Melania Trump for her involvement in last month's Kherson region ceasefire, which allowed for the evacuation of hundreds of civilians from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
The Russian president then proposed organising a similar five-day ceasefire for Kostyantynivka, a contested front-line Ukrainian city in the eastern region of Donetsk.
Kyiv disputes that Russia fully holds the town, and a truce could help Moscow's troops to make a final push to seize it.

"Considering that they brought in equipment and rotated troops in Oleshky under the guise of a humanitarian operation, it's clear what they want in Kostyantynivka," Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmitry Lytvyn said, adding that the details would need to be "clarified".

The separate in-person meetings with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents were only announced on Wednesday after two days of talks which were framed as centred around the postwar security architecture of Europe.

Nearly five years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow shows no sign of backing down from its maximalist demands for sovereign Ukrainian territory and for Western countries to give up any future commitment to protecting Kyiv in case of further attacks.

On Thursday, Putin again repeated that the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine was "unacceptable" to Russia, and said Russia would like the Americans to engage with Europe "so that the Europeans can decide what they truly want: peace or war".
During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly.

However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table.

The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture.
Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations.
But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle.

Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses".

articles.headline: Jensen Huang is out. What did China want from him?
keyFacts: Today, we’re talking about the Jensen Huang scandal at Nvidia, which is developing so quickly that we had to do an emergency update of this intro minutes before publishing this episode.
